question: Does the server survive startup when /tmp is a small tmpfs that takes the 1 MiB staging probe but not a copy of the mailbox family?

setup.container: ubuntu:26.04 (sha256:6e92c4fd8dfdf7276d56743a65002a91c9eb35dbe7af327e6c85bd204b646156), --read-only root, --user host uid, entrypoint mcp-agent-mail serve --no-tui with the published image's environment (HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0, STORAGE_ROOT=/data/mailbox, TUI_ENABLED=false, AM_INTERFACE_MODE=mcp, RUST_LOG=info) plus HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN
setup.binary: bind-mounted read-only at /usr/local/bin/mcp-agent-mail; ubuntu:26.04 instead of the published Debian 13 image because main release builds need GLIBC_2.43
setup.mailbox: built by v0.3.38 itself over MCP (1 project, 2 agents, 81 messages with 30 KB bodies), stopped gracefully; storage.sqlite3 2,867,200 B, -wal 5,141,792 B, -shm 32,768 B
setup.tmpfs: /tmp size = staged family pages (1967) + 4 pages = 8,073,216 B, the reporter's shape (4,092 of 4,096 pages used)

shapes.inplace: the original mailbox directory: the native staging path copies the family without -shm, the copy fits, and opening it maps a fresh -shm
shapes.copy: cp -a of the same mailbox: inode identity changes, the namespace record no longer matches, the raw staging path also copies -shm and runs out of space

fix.commit: 2dd72851 + this change (the two doc comments split for clippy after the build; no code difference)

results.outcome: exit 135 (SIGBUS) after startup; last log line the WAL-FEC WARN, exactly the reporter's symptom
up and serving after 40 s; graceful stop exit 0
results.log: Temp directory /tmp cannot hold mailbox probe copies (no space left on device for a private probe copy: /tmp has 7884 KiB free, the mailbox family needs about 9020 KiB); staging them under /data/mailbox/diagnostics/staging instead. Free space there or point TMPDIR at a writable filesystem.

results.outcome: exit 1: the staging ENOSPC was read as mailbox damage, the database was reconstructed from the archive, then promotion failed on the same ENOSPC (br-txx8u, fixed on main after v0.3.38)
exit 1, no reconstruction: 'Database sanity probe could not run because the host is out of disk space ... mailbox health could not be determined'
up and serving after 40 s; same staging-fallback warning as inplace; graceful stop exit 0
up and serving; no warning; no diagnostics/staging directory created, so a temp directory with room keeps staging

earlier_controls: published ghcr v0.3.38 image (sha256:cc1424e79d4ea2f912a17da754e168a3a75ff656cc112c06fdfa5d465a8df3f7), in place, same tmpfs sizing: exit 135
published ghcr v0.3.38 image, same mailbox, 64 MiB tmpfs: healthy
published ghcr v0.3.38 image, copied mailbox, 256 MiB tmpfs: healthy (copying a mailbox is not itself a fault)
not_covered: a storage filesystem that is itself too full for the fallback: covered only by the unit test staging_root_keeps_the_temp_directory_when_no_location_has_room (startup keeps /tmp, and each staging call then refuses with StorageFull instead of crashing)
the engine root cause: FrankenSQLite extends -shm sparsely before MAP_SHARED, so a live mailbox whose own filesystem fills can still SIGBUS (Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite#506)
